name: The Charnel House
summary: Four oak ossuary racks of stacked long bones and rows of skulls, a small altar with a candle, and the charnel cart that brings more.
description: When the churchyard fills, the old graves are dug up and the bones come here. They are stacked with a clerk's tidiness: long bones laid lengthwise on the shelves of four oak racks, a row of skulls along the front of each shelf looking out at the room. A small altar against the east wall keeps a candle burning for all of them at once. The charnel cart in the south-west corner is loaded for the next shelf. The dead were buried with rings and the diggers were not always thorough, so here and there a gap in a skull row holds something small and bright that a relative left, or a digger hid.
build: Shell: the kit's Crypt shell, 12.0 × 12.0 × 0.30 m slab, 0.50 m dressed-sandstone walls 3.00 m clear, a 0.45 m dark trim course, an archway 2.60 × 2.16 m centred on every wall.

Racks: four oak ossuary racks 3.00 m long (|x| 2.20 … 5.20), 0.50 m deep against the north and south walls, 2.10 m tall: two end posts and three shelves 0.05 m at 0.10, 0.80 and 1.50 m above the floor.
Bone stacks: on every shelf a stack of long bones 2.70 × 0.34 × 0.15 m laid lengthwise at the back.
Skulls: seven to a shelf along the front edge on top of the stack, each an eight-sided drum r 0.10 m, 0.16 m deep, facing the room.
Gaps: on one shelf of each rack (NE and SW the top, NW and SE the middle) the middle skull is missing; the loot anchor sits in the gap on the bone stack.
Altar (NE): sandstone 0.60 × 0.90 × 1.00 m against the east wall at y 2.90, an iron candlestick and candle on it.

Charnel cart (SW): an oak bed 1.20 × 0.70 m, 0.10 m thick, top 0.95 m above ground at (−3.60, −3.00), two spoked wheels r 0.30 m on an iron axle, a leg and a handle to the west; a load of bones 1.00 × 0.50 m on it.
The crossing: bare floor between all four archways.
sockets: Archway ×4, centred on each wall: 2.60 × 2.16 m (Crypt), all open
Skull-row gaps: four loot anchors, one per rack

The racks line the north and south walls; the crossing is open and exposed.
